pred_reasoning_trace: An 86-year-old woman with a history of dementia, living in a non–air-conditioned room during a heat wave, was found unconscious and brought to the emergency department. On arrival, her Glasgow Coma Scale score was 6 (E1V1M4), body temperature 42.4 °C, blood pressure 88/40 mm Hg, and pulse rate 120 beats/min. Laboratory studies revealed hepatic dysfunction, renal dysfunction, and disseminated intravascular coagulation. Head MRI and MRA showed no abnormality. She was diagnosed with severe heat stroke (APACHE II score 42, SOFA score 15), intubated, and treated with extracorporeal cooling, fluid resuscitation, and DIC therapy; fursultiamine and levothyroxine were also given. Despite treatment, she remained unconscious. On day 6, brain MRI showed bilateral cerebellar hemisphere high-signal intensity on diffusion-weighted and FLAIR images with corresponding low ADC signals. On day 9, SPECT with 123I-IMP demonstrated decreased perfusion in the right cerebellar hemisphere. By day 13, MRI abnormalities had begun to improve, and her level of consciousness improved to E4VTM6.
